newsitem.title: USA: Weatherford CEO comfortable with estimates.
newsitem.headline: Weatherford CEO comfortable with estimates.

text.p: Weatherford Enterra Inc chief executive officer Thomas Amonett said the company was "comfortable" with estimates that it would earn $1.83 a share in 1997.
"We've said we're comfortable with that (figure)," he told Reuters after the oilfield service company's annual meeting. The estimate was compiled by First Call.

Amonett also said the company was nearing completion of a streamlining plan announced last September to sell off four business units: Arrow Completion Systems, CRC-Evans Pipeline, Total Engineering Services Team and American Aero Cranes.
Arrow Completions Systems was sold in December and the sale of CRC-Evans Pipeline is expected to close by the end of May, Amonett said.
A definitive agreement to sell Total Engineering Services Team was signed last week, with the expectation that the sale will be completed in June, he said.
"We are in the final throes of negotiations with the purchaser of the crane business (American Aero Crane) and we expect to sign an agreemeent with them in the next few weeks," Amonett said.
He did not comment on purchasers or prices or how the sales would affect Weatherford Enterra's earnings. In 1996, the company earned $1.35 a share on revenues of $995 million.
Amonett has been interim president and CEO for Weatherford since last summer and will be replaced on July 1 by Thomas Bates.
